instructions: Generate missing files only, built-in imagegen, one at a time; save to assets/environment/island/ with exact filenames. Inspect local references before use. Rims genuine transparent alpha; top textures opaque. Original top_<biome>.png is A; generate B,C,D for four total. Preserve originals and drafts. No placement/code edits. Read the mirrored geometry and high-ground side carefully. Images here are new assets, not implementations of connected ranges, shared corner calibration, blending or water rendering. Lake-edge prompts are separately in lake_edges_prompts.json and the Markdown image doc.
sharedRimPrompt: Semi-realistic painted illustration, muted moody colours, soft overcast light from the upper left, 1870s Japan. Classic 2:1 isometric game view: camera looks down at about 27 degrees from the south-east; ground diagonals slope one down for two across. Same detailed painted materials, natural olive foliage and weathered stone as the supplied approved rim and game pine. Trees about 200 pixels wide at 1536 × 1024. A single modular low rim strip on genuine transparent alpha, no backdrop, no ground plane beyond the described narrow high-ground strip, no cast background shadow, text, border or frame. Keep lighting upper-left and tree/rock scale consistent. This supplies the missing opposite-bank orientation, not a taller cliff. Match the approved rim's length and low local height; clean ends for linking, no rounded island or endcaps.
sharedTexturePrompt: Semi-realistic painted terrain texture for the same 1870s Japanese island game, muted moody palette and fine natural material detail matching the supplied approved high-ground texture. STRICT ORTHOGRAPHIC TOP-DOWN, camera straight down at 90 degrees, NOT isometric: show only plan-view crowns and rock/ground surfaces, no tree trunks, side silhouettes, standing cliffs or horizon. 1024 × 1024 opaque PNG filling every pixel. Seamless/tileable: all opposite edges continue naturally, no border, vignette, edge fading, text or baked directional cast shadows. One continuous terrain texture, NOT a sheet or grid of several tiles. Match the reference's fine-feature scale, mean colour, brightness and contrast so the four variants can blend into a natural mosaic. Avoid obvious stripes, rows, a central focal feature and large unique repeated motifs.
